## Design

### 2026-10-04 — I started the YAZ Desk Hub project by planning a small robot-inspired desk companion to help with focus sessions. I created a master roadmap covering the product design, electronics, firmware, enclosu

**2h**

I started the YAZ Desk Hub project by planning a small robot-inspired desk companion to help with focus sessions. I created a master roadmap covering the product design, electronics, firmware, enclosure, testing, and budget.
Next, I designed the robot’s appearance using Higgsfield. The concept is a compact, rounded desk device with a tilted OLED screen for its pixel face and timer, one top button, a small status light, and USB-C power. The proposed colors are warm off-white, charcoal, and teal. The render is a visual concept, not a finished CAD model or physical prototype.
I also researched a first-build parts list. The proposed core includes an ESP32 development board, a 128×64 monochrome OLED, a tactile button, and a small piezo buzzer. The board’s built-in RGB light can indicate status, so a separate RGB LED and optional temperature/humidity sensor can wait until later. I drafted a starting pin plan for the display, button, and buzzer.
One challenge is the budget: the example prices for the main parts already come close to or exceed $30 once a USB cable and basic building supplies are included. Those are online prices, not confirmed prices delivered to Morocco, so I still need to check local availability and the real total cost. I also need to verify the exact parts and their voltage compatibility before wiring them.
The robot has not been physically built yet. My next steps are to source the parts, test them on a breadboard, write the timer and display code, and then design an enclosure based on the real component measurements. I’ll consider a custom PCB after the prototype works.
